nodes.label: Five Design Rules
nodes.rationale: Words first. Redundancy on every hazard. Big and few. Ivory on near-black. Nothing animates that carries meaning. The brand voice is a safety instrument, not a lifestyle app.

nodes.label: Document Precedence
nodes.rationale: When documents disagree, AGENTS.md wins over CODE_REFERENCE.md. When any document disagrees with the shipped code, the code wins. For design tokens, design.md wins over Theme.swift and WatchTheme.swift. Screen layout and button labels follow the shipped code and the tests that pin them.

nodes.label: Voice-Primary Thesis
nodes.rationale: Every function must be reachable by one spoken utterance. The screen is a spotter's dashboard and a safety net, never the only way. The phone is clamped to the cane, so a VoiceOver scan of many controls is a bad trade while walking.

nodes.label: Head Height Warning
nodes.rationale: "Head height." is spoken at the onset of a head episode and once more only under 0.6 m. It is never delayed behind a direction: a walker reaches a 1.5 m overhang in about 1.5 s. Muse rejected holding the words behind a playing direction.

nodes.label: Speech Priorities
nodes.rationale: Bands are .scene < .obstacle < .nav < .safety. Two .safety lines never cut each other. The .head haptic is never suppressed or delayed. A cut line resumes from its clause. Bands are separated by a 0.35 s pause that a safety line never waits for.

nodes.label: Critical-Only Speech
nodes.rationale: Speech is event-driven. Nothing speaks on a timer except the arrival hint. Beacon and haptics carry continuous guidance so speech stays the exception. Headphone audio can mask traffic, echolocation, and voices.

nodes.label: HeadGate
nodes.rationale: A lane is an overhang when the head cell is near and the torso cell is invalid or at least 0.5 m farther. The owner decided the signature ships ON. Step 52 shipped band re-fires at 1.0 and 0.6 m and a 2 s trusted-clear episode end. The closing requirement for the onset line was not shipped, because hard rule 8 says the onset always speaks.

nodes.label: Cue Safety Floor
nodes.rationale: Every overhang episode gets its haptic and one "Head height." at onset, at every verbosity level. The hush gesture does not affect it.

nodes.label: Mount Aim 3 to 8 Degrees
nodes.rationale: The Mount card should read good at 3–8 degrees below the horizon. Steeper than about 10 degrees and the lanes see pavement. Level or up and the drop-off detector loses its ground reference.

nodes.label: Voice Safety Floor
nodes.rationale: "Head height.", LiDAR ground hazards, and the .head haptic are not switchable by voice at any cue level. .safety breaks through the voice hold. A cue must never wait behind recognition or the 2.5 s voice race.

nodes.label: Overhang Signature
nodes.rationale: HeadGate ships ON by owner decision. A head cue requires the torso cell invalid or at least a gap farther than the head cell, so walls the cane already finds are not called head height. An uncovered torso cell still warns.

nodes.label: No Global Sign Cap
nodes.rationale: A global per-minute cap on signs was not added on purpose. It could suppress a critical sign such as SIDEWALK CLOSED. Per-phrase once-a-minute stands.

nodes.label: Overhangs Are the Real Gap
nodes.rationale: Do not tell the walker what the cane already tells them. Overhangs are rare, so a head alert has to mean a real overhang. Silence means all clear, so every cue must mean act now.

nodes.label: AppModel
nodes.rationale: Owns every engine and does the wiring. Pure decision types stay in CaneKitLogic; app classes own state, timing, and effects.

nodes.label: CueDecider
nodes.rationale: Pure cue state machine in CaneKitLogic. AppModel.handle turns its output into haptics, watch mirrors, and speech.

nodes.label: DepthFrameProcessor
nodes.rationale: Turns ARKit LiDAR frames into a LaneReport through the gyro gate, LaneMath, and mesh classification, about 30 Hz.

nodes.label: LaneReport
nodes.rationale: Value type the depth pipeline publishes. No coverage is .infinity plus a coverage flag, never NaN or -1, so every infinity-means-clear consumer stays correct.

nodes.label: NavigationEngine
nodes.rationale: Waypoint engine around GeofenceTracker, TurnSettle, OffCourseDetector, and CourseSmoother.

nodes.label: SpeechQueue
nodes.rationale: Single voice. Since Step 54 every line is cache, then a 2.5 s race, then the system voice only on failure.

nodes.label: Lane Ladder
nodes.rationale: TileLevel thresholds, not the view: clear at or beyond 2.0 m, far 1.2–2.0, near 0.7–1.2, urgent under 0.7, plus NO DATA and NO COVER. Every tile has a fill, a level word, and a number because colour alone fails deuteranopia.

nodes.label: Leaf Observation Isolation
nodes.rationale: Referencing a 15–30 Hz sensor property such as model.depth.report in ContentView.body makes SwiftUI re-evaluate the whole root hierarchy. Isolate those properties in leaf views such as ObstaclesCard and MountAimRow so only the views that render the data refresh.

nodes.label: ISR to CIF Demo Route
nodes.rationale: The demo route is ISR Townsend Hall to CIF on the UIUC campus (route_isr_cif.json). Any other destination uses MapKit walking directions.

nodes.label: Phone Is the Only Computer
nodes.rationale: An iPhone on a non-metal cane shaft does the sensing and the guidance. AirPods Pro and Apple Watch are optional channels. No ESP32 and no external sensors. The Mac only signs and installs.

nodes.label: 27.65 mm Cane Shaft
nodes.rationale: The prototype shaft is a 27.65 mm non-metal broom handle, measured by the bore-ring coupons. The old 28.75 mm figure is retired.

nodes.label: 12.7 mm Legacy Shaft
nodes.rationale: The drafts assume an Ambutech 12.7 mm aluminum or graphite shaft. The prototype stick is 27.65 mm non-metal, so none of these clamps fit it. The earlier 28.75 mm reading was wrong.

nodes.label: Beacon Only in Headphones
nodes.rationale: A spatial click from a speaker on a stick is noise. Speech continues on whatever output is connected. Head yaw is ignored until the first Recenter or auto-recenter.

nodes.label: Guided Access
nodes.rationale: Armed so a brush against the clamped screen cannot leave the app or hit Stop. While armed, the watch is the input. The screen stays on because ARKit stops if it locks.

nodes.label: Legacy ESP32 CAD Drafts
nodes.rationale: Do not print these for the demo. They are unrendered ESP32-era drafts (XIAO grip, VL53L1X pod, coin motors) sized for a 12.7 mm shaft. The phone-only CaneKit app replaced that plan. The live mount is hardware/mount_screwless.

nodes.label: AirPods and Watch Setup
nodes.rationale: AirPods and the watch are optional channels that must degrade, never break the walk. Nothing talks to the Mac at runtime.

nodes.label: System Spatial Audio Off
nodes.rationale: Turn system Spatial Audio and Head Tracking off. OpenCane does its own HRTF and its own head tracking. The system version fights it and recenters on its own schedule. Head tracking needs AirPods Pro, AirPods Max, or AirPods 3rd gen.

nodes.label: CaneKit
nodes.rationale: The code name: Xcode project, targets, scheme, PRODUCT_NAME CaneKit.app, the CaneKitLogic module, ios/CaneKit paths, Makefile targets, and CANEKIT_* variables. Renaming would not change anything a user sees.

nodes.label: CaneKitLogic
nodes.rationale: Pure Foundation decisions with numbers (metres, seconds, degrees, Hz) live in ios/Logic with tests. NavigationEngine, SpeechQueue, and HapticPlayer only own state and timing around those types.

nodes.label: Frozen Bundle IDs
nodes.rationale: com.aritro.canekit, .watchkitapp, and .widget stay frozen. iOS keys the install, permissions, UserDefaults, Documents, and the ElevenLabs cache off the bundle id. A new id installs a second app and spends another of the 10 weekly personal-team App IDs.

nodes.label: OpenCane
nodes.rationale: The name a person sees and hears: CFBundleDisplayName, Guide nav title, watch title, spoken lines, usage strings, and Siri phrases via applicationName.

nodes.label: Spoken OpenCane, Code CaneKit
nodes.rationale: AppIntents use the display name through applicationName, so the spoken name is OpenCane. Code names stay CaneKit.

nodes.label: Four Tabs
nodes.rationale: Guide, Details, Settings, and Profile. The Guide title is OpenCane. The Details case is still .sense. The root tab bar is icon-only; words exist for VoiceOver.

nodes.label: OpenCane vs CaneKit Name Split
nodes.rationale: The two names are deliberate, not a half-finished rename. Spoken or visible strings say OpenCane. Types, files, modules, targets, paths, schemes, and the bundle id stay CaneKit. Changing CFBundleDisplayName changes the Siri phrase to "in OpenCane". "OpenCane ready." is VoiceShellPolicy.readyLine and is matched by bytes.

nodes.label: Voice-Only Mode Ships Off
nodes.rationale: The voice-only layout removes secondary controls. It ships off because "the walker can no longer reach Recenter with a finger" needs a mounted walk before it is a default. One pure CaneKitLogic type answers which controls are visible.

nodes.label: Not Directed at Children Under 13
nodes.rationale: OpenCane is not directed at children under 13 and does not knowingly collect their information.

nodes.label: Always-Free Safety Surface
nodes.rationale: Obstacle detection, haptics, audio, navigation, and emergency calling are never gated. Safety features cannot sit behind a purchase.

nodes.label: Name People Ahead
nodes.rationale: Premium switch for advanced AI object detection. Off by default until tuned on the cane.

nodes.label: OpenCane Premium
nodes.rationale: Step 69.5 PremiumGate locks exactly three switches: Hazard watch, Name people ahead, and Alert my family. Obstacle detection, haptics, audio, navigation, and emergency calling stay free. Product opencane_premium_annual is $49.99/year with a one-month free intro in OpenCane.storekit. Every Premium line is spoken at .scene.

nodes.label: RevenueCat purchases-ios
nodes.rationale: The one owner-approved third-party package, linked by the app target only and imported only by EntitlementManager.swift. It never touches the cue path, the audio session, haptics, or the depth pipeline.

nodes.label: opencane_premium_annual
nodes.rationale: Annual product at $49.99 with a one-month free introductory offer. Entitlement premium. Offering default. The paywall does not open during a walk.

nodes.label: PremiumGate
nodes.rationale: Premium.swift decides what OpenCane Premium unlocks and when the paywall may appear. entitlementID premium, productID opencane_premium_annual, offeringID default. notConfigured unlocks everything. Three features (hazardWatch, namePeople, familyAlerts) map onto two paywall benefits (advancedDetection, familyAlerts).

nodes.label: Demo Free-Month Line
nodes.rationale: After the walk stops, the paywall is filmed showing "The first month is free." and $49.99/year, plus the line that navigation and obstacle detection are always free.

nodes.label: Mid-Walk Premium Refusal
nodes.rationale: While walking, Details then Hazard watch shows no paywall. The cane says "Premium features can be turned on after this walk." Stop the route, then the paywall appears.

nodes.label: OpenCane Premium Paywall
nodes.rationale: Gated switches are Hazard watch, Name people ahead, and Alert my family. A mid-walk tap is refused with "Premium features can be turned on after this walk." at .scene. An open paywall closes when a walk starts. The paywall itself makes no sound and no haptic.

nodes.label: People Counting
nodes.rationale: Named here as a Premium addition alongside Hazard watch. Other docs call the same switch Name people ahead.

nodes.label: Walk Lock
nodes.rationale: The index points the walk lock at AppModel+Premium.swift. The paywall does not open during a walk.

nodes.label: On-Device Safety Data
nodes.rationale: Obstacle detection, head-height warnings, drop-off warnings, and sign reading run on the phone. Camera frames for those features are not stored or uploaded. Trip logs stay in the Files app.

nodes.label: EntitlementManager
nodes.rationale: The only file that imports RevenueCat purchases-ios. Without a RevenueCat key every feature is unlocked.

nodes.label: Premium.swift
nodes.rationale: CaneKitLogic gate for OpenCane Premium. Numeric premium rules live here with the rest of CaneKitLogic.

nodes.label: OpenCane.storekit
nodes.rationale: Local StoreKit configuration for opencane_premium_annual at $49.99 with a one-month free introductory offer, selected by the CaneKit scheme Run action. Purchases can be tested without App Store Connect.

nodes.label: Free-Month Eligibility Rule
nodes.rationale: The paywall says "The first month is free." only when RevenueCat reports IntroEligibilityStatus.eligible (EntitlementManager.freeTrialPeriod). .ineligible and .unknown keep the charge-at-subscribe wording. The introductory offer still exists after it has been used, so eligibility is asked per Apple Account. CANEKIT_PAYWALL_PREVIEW=1 forces the free month for the screenshot tour only.

nodes.label: Missing RevenueCat Key Unlocks Everything
nodes.rationale: A build without REVENUECAT_API_KEY is .notConfigured and unlocks every feature. Automated launches (CANEKIT_UITEST, CANEKIT_MUTE, --demo-route) do the same even if a key is present, unless CANEKIT_PREMIUM=free|premium forces a state. That keeps XCUITests, the tour, e2e, and a fresh clone behaving as before.

nodes.label: Walk Lock
nodes.rationale: The paywall never opens during a walk. AppModel.requestPaywall(for:) refuses while isWalkActive. RootView closes an open paywall when a walk starts. A lapse mid-walk waits until the walk ends. Nothing is revoked or unlocked mid-walk.

nodes.label: Free-Trial Paywall Wording
nodes.rationale: PaywallPricing.spokenOffer appends "The first period is free." only when the caller passes a period. The caller passes a period only when this Apple Account is eligible. Without a period, renewal terms say the charge is when you subscribe.

nodes.label: Onboarding Omits Premium
nodes.rationale: Onboarding never shows a paywall, a price, or the word Premium. First launch asks for camera, location, and microphone under a line that says why.

nodes.label: Free-Month Eligibility Rule
nodes.rationale: The first month is free only for an Apple Account that can still redeem the introductory offer. The offer still exists after someone has used it, so the paywall asks RevenueCat whether this account is eligible before promising a free month. Returning customers see the charge-at-subscribe terms. VoiceOver reads "The first month is free" only when that account is eligible.

nodes.label: Safety Is Not for Sale
nodes.rationale: Safety features cannot sit behind a purchase. The subscription is the extra awareness and the family loop, and it waits until the person is standing still.

nodes.label: No Paywall During a Walk
nodes.rationale: A paywall during a walk is a safety problem. The gate refuses Premium switches while a route is active and closes the sheet if a walk starts. Turn Hazard watch on mid-route and the cane says to finish the walk first.

nodes.label: Free-Month Eligibility Rule
nodes.rationale: EntitlementManager shows the free month only when IntroEligibilityStatus.eligible. The local product is opencane_premium_annual at $49.99/year with a free P1M intro.

nodes.label: Walk Lock
nodes.rationale: The paywall does not open during a walk. The walk lock is AppModel+Premium.swift. The gate is Premium.swift, the store client is EntitlementManager.swift, and the screen is PaywallView.swift.
